title: Require close-out handoff in worker and execution skills
description:
Why this issue exists
The executing-plans and bead-worker skills instruct agents to validate and close beads, but they do not explicitly require the canonical close-out boundary: update Beads notes, run git status, report changed files and validation, capture follow-up work, then close only when acceptance criteria are met.

What needs to be done
Update plugins/gin-workflow/src/skills/executing-plans/SKILL.md and plugins/gin-workflow/src/skills/bead-worker/SKILL.md so both defer to docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md before closure. Make it clear that validation success alone is insufficient without handoff evidence and Beads outcome notes.
acceptance_criteria: executing-plans and bead-worker both reference the canonical verification-and-handoff workflow before closure. Both require git status and handoff evidence before bd close. Both explain that failed or incomplete validation leaves the bead in progress or blocked with notes.
notes: Updated executing-plans and bead-worker skills to defer closure to docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md, require Beads outcome notes plus git status and handoff evidence before bd close, and keep failed/incomplete work in progress or blocked with notes. Verified by targeted doc review and text checks.

title: Prevent orchestrator closure before integration close-out
description:
Why this issue exists
The bead-orchestrator skill currently closes a bead when a worker finishes successfully, then performs worktree safety checks and integration afterward. This can mark durable Beads state as complete before integration, verification, handoff, and follow-up capture are actually done.

What needs to be done
Update the orchestrator guidance so worker success produces a ready-for-close result, but final bd close happens only after required safety checks, integration when in scope, verification evidence, handoff context, and follow-up work capture are complete. Align wording with docs/agent-task-lifecycle.md and docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md.
acceptance_criteria: bead-orchestrator does not instruct agents to close before integration or close-out checks. Closure wording explicitly follows verification-and-handoff workflow. Any integration failure leaves the bead active or blocked with notes rather than closed.
notes: Updated bead-orchestrator so worker success means ready for integration and close-out review, not immediate closure. Final bd close now depends on the canonical verification-and-handoff workflow, integration completion when in scope, Beads outcome notes, git status review, follow-up capture, and handoff evidence. Verified by targeted doc review and text checks.

title: Consolidate gin-workflow plugins
description: Consolidate the current core and advanced plugin split into one plugin named gin-workflow. Remove redundant commands and skills while keeping only core and high-value workflow capabilities. Approved direction: keep a codebase technical-documentation capability as /tech-doc, and strengthen /plan into a requirement-analysis workflow that discusses, clarifies, compares approaches, and finalizes a high-quality durable implementation plan before orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: Repository exposes one plugin with a minimal command/skill set. Installer/docs no longer reference a separate advanced plugin or --plugin core|advanced split. Retained commands include plan, orchestrate, execute, verify, progress, ship, beads-status, and tech-doc. /plan analyzes requirements, asks clarifying questions, proposes approaches/tradeoffs, gets user alignment, then writes an orchestration-ready plan. /tech-doc scans the codebase and writes a human-readable technical document covering tech stack, architecture design, database design, code structure, code conventions, concerns, quality risks, and follow-up Beads. Removed redundant surfaces leave no broken references.
notes: Next-session implementation notes: remove plugins/gin-workflow-advanced; merge any retained high-value review/debug skills into plugins/gin-workflow if still desired; remove /quick, /new-project, and old /map-codebase in favor of /tech-doc; update install.sh to target only gin-workflow and remove --plugin core|advanced|all semantics or make it a no-op compatibility alias; update README to document a single plugin; update /plan and writing-plans to require requirement analysis, clarification, tradeoff discussion, recommended approach, user alignment, and durable plan generation; add tech-doc command/skill backed by codebase-mapper; verify with install dry-runs and broken-reference search.

title: Audit current workflow surfaces and assumptions
description: Review README, AGENTS/CLAUDE instructions, slash commands, workflow skills, hooks, scripts, and existing review residuals to identify where the agent lifecycle is duplicated, ambiguous, or inconsistent with Beads as source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: Audit notes identify current lifecycle entry points, task-state stores, handoff rules, duplicated guidance, and concrete pain points to address.
notes: Audit completed in docs/workflow-audit-2026-07-08.md. Key findings: workflow entry points are split across README, AGENTS, CLAUDE, commands, and skills; durable task state conflicts between Beads and .planning/orchestration-state.json; execution/completion guidance is duplicated across repo rules and plugin commands; AGENTS mixes bd and br workflows while br is unavailable in this workspace. Recommended follow-up centers on p80.1, p80.3, p80.4, p80.6, and p80.7.

title: Define target agent task lifecycle
description: Specify the intended discover -> claim -> plan -> implement -> verify -> handoff lifecycle for agents, including when to use Beads, local plans, worktrees, subagents, and persistent memory.
design: Canonical lifecycle spec is in docs/agent-task-lifecycle.md. Model guidance will be plan metadata only: abstract classes high_reasoning, standard_impl, cheap_simple; standard_impl is the implicit default; brainstorm/design/review prefer high_reasoning; plan defaults to standard_impl unless complexity justifies escalation; no Beads ownership and no hard enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Lifecycle spec defines phase boundaries, required commands, ownership/status transitions, blocked-work handling, and session-close behavior.
notes: Completed lifecycle and model-guidance alignment. Added docs/agent-task-lifecycle.md as canonical lifecycle spec, added .planning/plans/2026-07-09-model-class-planning-metadata.md, extended writing-plans/plan-schema.md with Model Guidance metadata, updated writing-plans skill and /plan command, and clarified README plus model-guidance design ownership. Model guidance remains plan metadata only; Beads remains durable task state.

title: Redesign agent workflow architecture
description: Create a durable initiative to redesign the gin-workflow agent lifecycle around Beads as the canonical task system, with repo docs serving as operating procedures and validation/handoff rules kept explicit.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed set of child issues covers audit, target lifecycle, Beads-backed orchestration, documentation, verification, and a simulated workflow test.

description: install_plugin() must validate that --project directory exists and resolve it to an absolute path before use. Old code had `[ ! -d \$PROJECT_DIR\ ]` check and `cd && pwd` normalization; both were dropped in the refactor.
acceptance_criteria: --project /nonexistent exits with error; --project . resolves to absolute path; generated hooks.json uses absolute paths

description: Split `local tmp_file=$(mktemp)` at lines 253 and 295 into separate `local tmp_file` declaration and `tmp_file=$(mktemp)` assignment so `set -e` catches mktemp failures. Shellcheck SC2155.
acceptance_criteria: local tmp_file=$(mktemp) at both lines 253 and 295 is split; shellcheck produces no SC2155 warnings
close_reason: Applied fixes for mktemp SC2155, PROJECT_DIR validation, Antigravity PLUGIN_ROOT, and Python heredoc hardening

title: Clarify Beads update versus closure sequence in close-out checklist
description:
Why this issue exists
The canonical verification-and-handoff workflow lists Update Beads before Prepare handoff summary, but its Beads update step also says to close only after handoff evidence is complete. The intended model is inferable, but the numbered sequence can lead agents to close too early.

What needs to be done
Revise docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md to separate interim Beads updates from final closure. The sequence should distinguish recording notes/blockers/follow-ups from running final bd close after handoff evidence is complete.
acceptance_criteria: The close-out sequence explicitly separates Beads notes/blocker/follow-up updates from final bd close. The final closure step comes after quality gates, Beads outcome notes, git status, and handoff summary. No wording implies bd close should happen before handoff evidence exists.
notes: Clarified docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md so Step 2 records Beads notes/blockers/follow-ups without closing early, and Step 5 is the only closure step after verification, git status, and handoff. Verified by doc review and targeted text checks.

title: Redesign orchestration state around Beads
description: Rework the conceptual orchestration model so Beads issues and dependencies are canonical for task state, while repo files such as orchestration-state.json are treated only as derived/session-local execution metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Design identifies which state belongs in Beads, which state may remain local/derived, how dependencies map to bd dep, and how progress commands should report status.

title: Separate human docs from agent execution instructions
description: Clarify documentation boundaries so README remains human-facing, AGENTS/CLAUDE files point to bd prime and operating policy, and command/skill files contain actionable agent execution rules without duplicating task lists.
acceptance_criteria: Docs have explicit ownership boundaries, avoid duplicated task-tracking instructions, and consistently direct durable work state to Beads.

title: Add verification and handoff checklist workflow
description: Define or update the workflow so agents run relevant quality gates, update/close Beads, inspect git status, and report changed files, validation, blocked items, and proposed next commands without committing or pushing unless authorized.
acceptance_criteria: Verification and handoff rules are explicit, non-interactive, platform-aware, and aligned with the repository's conservative/minimal Beads profile.
notes: Drafted canonical close-out workflow in docs/verification-and-handoff-workflow.md and aligned verification-before-completion, finishing-a-development-branch, /verify, and /ship to defer to it. The checklist now makes quality gates, Beads updates, git status, non-interactive handoff contents, and conservative no-commit/no-push behavior explicit.

notes: Validated the redesigned lifecycle with simulated bead gin-workflow-brr. Added docs/workflow-validation-simulation-2026-07-09.md capturing discover, claim, plan, implement, verify, handoff, and close. No new blocking architectural gaps were found.

title: Harden Python inline scripts against special chars in paths
description: Three python3 -c blocks at lines 300, 325, 350 expand shell variables directly into Python string literals. A single-quote in a path name would break the Python syntax. Pass path values as CLI arguments or use heredoc to avoid string interpolation injection.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin names with special characters do not cause Python SyntaxError; paths passed safely to Python
close_reason: Applied fixes for mktemp SC2155, PROJECT_DIR validation, Antigravity PLUGIN_ROOT, and Python heredoc hardening

Acceptance Criteria
- A small artifact is created under docs/.
- The task is claimed, planned, implemented, verified, and closed using the current documented workflow.
- Notes capture what was verified and any friction observed.
